title: Work the Exception Queue
scenario: It is 1:00 PM. Four invoices were held at the fork, each for a different reason. Working an exception is not deleting it - it is routing each one to the owner who can resolve it and logging what happens. Assign the four correctly so nothing is silently dropped.
input: INV-59002 - price over tolerance (bills $1,230 vs PO $1,140). INV-58962 - duplicate (already paid day-0). INV-59004 - vendor V-1205 not in master. INV-59005 - missing receipt (two-way only). Owners available: AP Clerk, Procurement Lead, Vendor Relations Desk, Receiving Desk.
instructions: Treat each held invoice as work to route, not to discard.
Match each exception to the owner who can actually resolve it.
Answer the routing questions and validate to mint the exception resolution log.

questions.prompt: INV-59002 was held for a price over tolerance. Who works it?

options.text: The Receiving Desk, to re-count the goods
The Procurement Lead, who owns the PO and can confirm or correct the agreed price
The vendor, who set the price

questions.explain: A price dispute is about what was agreed on the PO. The Procurement Lead owns the register, so they confirm the price or resolve the difference before the invoice can proceed.

questions.prompt: INV-58962 was flagged as a duplicate of a day-0 payment. What is the resolution?

options.text: Pay it again to be safe
Reject it - it was already paid; the AP Clerk records the rejection
Send it to Procurement for a new PO

questions.explain: A confirmed duplicate must not pay twice. The AP Clerk rejects it and logs why, closing the exception with a clear record rather than letting it linger.

questions.prompt: INV-59004's vendor V-1205 is not in the master. Who must act first?

options.text: The AP Clerk, by paying to a temporary account
The Vendor Relations Desk, to onboard and verify the vendor before payment is possible

questions.explain: Payment is impossible without a governed vendor record. Vendor Relations owns onboarding, so they verify and add V-1205 - and only then can the invoice re-enter the flow.

questions.prompt: INV-59005 was held for a missing receipt. What resolves it?

options.text: Waive the receipt since the price is fine
The Receiving Desk posts the goods receipt confirming delivery; until then it is held

questions.explain: The block is unproven delivery, not price. The Receiving Desk posts the receipt to confirm the goods arrived; the invoice stays held until that third leg exists.

copilotPrompt: Route four held invoices to their owners: a price-over-tolerance to Procurement, a duplicate to the AP Clerk to reject, an unknown vendor to Vendor Relations to onboard, and a missing receipt to the Receiving Desk to post.
successMessage: Exceptions routed. Four holds are assigned to owners and logged - none silently dropped.

intro.heading: Working exceptions: route and log, never drop

sections.title: An exception is work, not waste
sections.body: Holding an invoice does not resolve it. Each of the four held invoices needs an owner who can act - Procurement, the AP Clerk, Vendor Relations, or Receiving - and a logged outcome so it is not lost.

sections.title: The reason picks the owner
sections.body: Because the fork labeled each hold with its reason, routing is direct: a price gap goes to Procurement, a duplicate to the AP Clerk, an unknown vendor to Vendor Relations, a missing receipt to Receiving. The right desk resolves the right problem.

sections.title: Some exceptions can re-enter, some close
sections.body: A verified vendor or a posted receipt lets an invoice return to the flow; a confirmed duplicate is rejected and closed. Either way the resolution is recorded - that log is what makes the desk auditable.

takeaway.heading: Exception queue worked
points: You routed all four held invoices to the owner who can resolve each one.
The price dispute went to Procurement, the duplicate to the AP Clerk to reject, the unknown vendor to Vendor Relations, the missing receipt to Receiving.
Working an exception means routing and logging - nothing is silently dropped.
A resolved vendor or receipt can re-enter the flow; a confirmed duplicate is closed as rejected.
The workflow can now hand each exception to an accountable owner and keep an auditable record.
